mr_title: Removed casting from exact lookups in admin searches.
mr_description:
Instead of casting non-text fields to CharField (which prevents index
usage), skip exact lookups when the search term fails
formfield.to_python().

This preserves index usage for valid searches while gracefully handling
invalid search terms by simply not including them in the query for that
field.

For multi-term searches like 'foo 123' on search_fields=['name', 'age__exact']:
- 'foo': invalid for age, so only name lookup is used
- '123': valid for both, so both lookups are used

This entails a slight increase in permissiveness for search terms that
can be normalized by formfield.to_python().

expected_issues.title: to_python() used as validator: crash on typed choices, over-match on booleans
expected_issues.description:
formfield().to_python() is not a validator for every field type: TypedChoiceField returns the raw string and forms.BooleanField maps almost any string to True, so search crashes (HTTP 500) or over-matches.

The new admin search skips exact lookups whose term fails formfield.to_python(). For fields with choices the form field is a TypedChoiceField whose to_python() does not coerce, so a term like 'john' against an IntegerField with choices reaches the ORM and raises ValueError in the changelist. For BooleanField, forms.BooleanField.to_python('anything') returns True, so any search term OR-matches every row with a True value instead of nothing. The validation needs strict, type-aware parsing (coerce for typed choices, strict boolean parsing).
